headline: Stiefel-constrained attention paper attributes CIFAR-10 gain to scale-free optimization step
summary: A v3 paper studies Stiefel-constrained query/key projections trained with a corrected Riemannian Adam update. On one CIFAR-10 image-patch benchmark at 10,000 examples, authors report a 6.79 percentage-point gain over AdamW across 12 paired starts; their 12-seed ablation attributes the improvement to a scale-free, step-capped update rather than to the tangent projector or equivariance. The optimizer took 1.82 seconds per epoch versus 0.73 seconds for the baseline. A separate modular-arithmetic grokking experiment finds no benefit for the constrained method; the paper’s positive grokking result is a single-seed pilot and remains unconfirmed. Independent replication and transfer to language-model training are open.
